properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.56(d) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to remove or fill pit within 9 months after completion of drilling or in accordance with extension granted by the Department without a Clean Streams Law permit or other approval under 25 Pa. Code Sections 78.57 or 78.58.
Violation ID: 8199417
Permit API: 129-23976
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/21/2024
Comments: On August 21 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Louis Yemc 1 Well in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. At the time of this inspection, the well site was exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the access road which remains unrestored. No active accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. Plugging operations appear to be completed. No equipment appears to be onsite and has been removed at the time of this inspection. The pit that was on site during plugging operations is now backfilled and is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the NOV response, which again included the requested Control and Disposal Plan, the Operator stated that:"The pit water was hauled away and used at another fracturing job by the contractor who was fracking in the area. The cement that was drilled out was encapsulated in the pit and buried. The Operator also stated that after one day, there was not water. That cement was created when we had to drill out and re-cement this well. The contractor that the Operator hired was confident that there is no water run off anywhere on location."However, under 25 PA Code 78.62(a)(1), disposal of residual wastes in pits may occur at the well site if the waste is generated by the drilling or production of an oil or gas well located on the well site. Additionally, under 25 PA Code 78.56(4)(d), pits used during servicing, plugging and recompleting the well shall be removed or filled within 90 days of construction. Therefore, the encapsulation of the residual waste and pit used during plugging of the well is not in compliance with 25 PA Code 78.62(a)(1) and 25 PA Code 78.56(4)(d). If the access road is to remain the Department requests the following information in regards to the access road:1. Map of area being proposing to remain including if there would PCSM proposed in that area.2. Map or overlay of how site was to be restored.3. Include property boundaries.The Department requests an NOV response to be provided to the Department by 9/4/2024. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding for failure to remove the pit. The well site and access road appear to be permanently stabilized at this time, violations are being closed for failure to implement Erosion and Sediment BMPs(Best Management Practices).

Violation ID: 8230686
Permit API: 063-33033
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/24/2025
Comments: The Department received a complaint on 3/5/2025 that there were E and S issues with the access road for the Samual Serian 1 1470 well. On 3/10/2025, I conducted a complaint inspection of Diversified Production, LLC's Samuel Serian 1 1470 well (API 063-33033) in Grant Twp., Indiana County. During my inspection, I observed numerous areas of accelerated erosion. Violations were cited for the erosion and sedimentation issues with the access road. A Notice of Violation was sent on 3/20/2025, and Diversified sent a response on 3/28/2025. On 4/11/2025, Brian Shank (WQSS) and I met Heather Empfield, AJ Smith and John Stibrik at the access road for the Samual Serian 1 1470 well. We discussed different ideas to address the culvert and eroding access road. Today, Brian Shank, Samantha Lutz (Aquatic Biologist 2), Danielle Zimmerman (Environmental Engineer) and I met at the access road for the Samual Serian 1 1470 well. The Department recommends submitting a GP11 to replace the culvert and repair the access road. The existing 4 culvert pipes will need to be replaced with a single pipe. The outstanding violations from the 3/10/2025 complaint inspection will remain open.

Inspection Date: 2/23/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to being notified by Craig Vanderhoof (operator of well) of a crude oil release due to a compromised underground gathering line adjacent to this conventional well, that was discovered on 2/21/26. It is estimated that approximately 10-20 gallons of crude oil was released onto the well site.Since the discovery of the release, the compromised line has been replaced and absorbents and a vac truck were used to collect the released product. The remediation measures that have already occurred and remain in place (absorbent diapers, booms) appear sufficient. I advised Craig to monitor the remediated area during upcoming warmups and rainfall events to ensure any residual crude is collected by the remaining absorbents.

Comments: On 03/14/2024, I responded to a formal complaint (CTS# 378891). The complaint description included environmental concerns at a compressor station, visible spills and no containment at well sites. During my investigation at this well site, I found TJ Allshouse unloading a small bulldozer. The well and compressor station in the complaint are owned and operated by Mr. Allshouse. The Smosna 1 well is a conventional well, a containment dike is in place around the brine tank near this well. Mr. Allshouse said the well has been shut in over winter. Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed through a culvert under the access road and continued to spread out and flow through vegetation approximately 400 feet. Moody & Associates has been employed to coordinate the clean-up of this crude oil release. Jordan Sipos, P.G. completed the testing to establish the extent of the release and contaminated soil. Clean-up of the contaminated soil has been ongoing and is nearly completed. Several piles of contaminated soil have been secured adjacent to the clean-up area until testing has been completed for disposal. Due to recent precipitation events removal of the remaining contaminated soil has been delayed. Work crew on site at the time of this inspection. The removal of the contaminated soil was completed with the least disturbance possible to the surrounding vegetation and without creating a muddy unstable area. Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. Manifest for the removal and disposal of the contaminated soil need to be submitted to the Department to lift the violations associated with this release. 15 Day initial Response Letter received July 1, 2019 for Alternate Remediation provision found in the PA DEP Oil and Gas Spill Policy.

Inspection Date: 6/27/2022
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on Pad B following a report from the operator of a release of 140 barrels to secondary containment which overflowed the containment on 6/24/2022. I met with company men Mike Hood and Yadir Lozano upon arriving on location They both accompanied me on this inspection. They showed me the location on the pad where the blender had released produced water to the secondary containment. They also showed me the flow path that the release took once it had overflowed containment. The release flowed to the north where it entered the stormwater channel along the northern side of the pad. It then flowed both west and east to both ends of the stormwater channel. The area around the northwest corner of the pad, where the stormwater channel begins, was dry at the time of this inspection. Fluid was observed seeping out of the gravel along the pad edge and into the north stormwater channel. A puddle in the stormwater channel had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 2.10 mS/cm near where these fluid seeps were observed. According to the company men, the release also flowed west over the pad surface and it flowed into the area that had been impacted by the release from 6/9/22. The EC of the fluid on the pad in this area was 4.08 mS/cm. Fluid was observed at the northeast corner of the pad where the north stormwater channel lets out. An EC reading of this fluid could not be taken due to the presence of a rattlesnake in the rocks in that area. On the pad surface near the northeast corner of the pad, I also found puddles with an EC of approximately 2 mS/cm. I recommended to the company men that these puddles be vacuumed up in addition to the other puddles present on the pad and in the north stormwater channel. I also observed a puddle of an oily substance with a green tint in the travel lane along the southern side of the pad. Company man Yadir Lozano said that this had been found just prior to my arrival on location and that they would excavate the impacted gravel material right away. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment. The tanks and containment appear to be in good condition. No issues noted on Pad A.Violations remain outstanding from the release on 6/24/22.

Comments: On 3/22/23 an incident inspection of the Veres Well Pad was conducted in response to a report of a spill reported to the Department on 3/22/23 (CTS: 370763).Background:On 3/22/23 I spoke to Keith Eighmey of Greylock to regarding a missed call from him the previous evening (3/21/23). Mr. Eighmey informed me that he had reported a spill to the Department hotline. The spill had occurred on the Veres Well Pad. According to Mr. Eighmey, an estimated 30 gallons of brine were released into an earthen containment berm. Greylock was in the process of removing the old tanks at the site to install new tanks with approved secondary containment. Two incidents resulted in the release. A small volume of brine mixed with sand and residual material was released when a manhole cover on the back of a tank was unbolted. Containment was being used at the time, but the volume of fluid mixed with the sediment overflowed out of the containment. Additionally, a vacuum truck was being used to draw down the tanks. The tank on the back of the truck was overfilled. When the suction was turned off, the excess fluid escaped back through the hose and onto the pad. I informed Mr. Eighmey that I would be coming out for a site inspection later the same day (3/22/23).The following was observed during the site inspection:-An Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo #1).-A crew was present excavating the spill area (Photo #2). According to Mr. Eighmey, they initially used ground liner containment yesterday to begin remediation efforts (Photo #3). However, Greylock has since acquired roll-off boxes and will transfer the waste that is currently on the liner into the boxes (Photo #4). -The old tanks were present and will be removed from the site (Photos #3 and #5-6).-A vacuum truck was present at the site (Photo #7).-Elevated conductivity was observed in pooled water that was slowly dripping from the sidecut of the excavated area (Photo #10).-Elevated conductivity was observed in a saturated layer of substrate below the gravel (Photos #8-9).-Elevated conductivity was not observed in the bottom of the excavated area (Photo #11). -No elevated conductivity was observed in the PCSM berms downslope of the release (Photos #12-13 and #17).-No elevated conductivity was observed at the drain outlet downslope of the release (Photos #15-16 and #17).According to Mr. Eighmey, they plan to continue excavation, install lined sump to monitor for the next few days to ensure full remediation. Additionally, Mr. Eighmey stated that Greylock is planning to follow 78a66(c)1 policy however, if further remediation efforts indicate that the release volume is greater than the initial estimate they will notify the Department and proceed with Act 2 procedures. Violations of 91.34(a), 78a57(a), 78a54, and SWMA 301 are being issued for the release.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2026
Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8270052
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/09/2026
Comments: On 04/09/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 42 degrees and sunny. Water Quality Specialist Korey Starkey and I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP traveled the area of the impact beginning at the release point (CTS #396090) (photo #2). The DEP was unable to field measure the Electrical Conductivity (EC) at the release point due to stimulation activities. The EC of the fluids up-gradient of the stormwater basin were ~ 240 us/cm (photo #3). The stormwater basin with containment has one 24/7 water truck recovering fluids on top of and underneath the containment and from the sumps. The EC of the fluids on top of the containment were ~ 277 us/cm (photo #4). The EC of the fluids in the sump located down gradient of where overflow pipe was located were ~ 742 us/cm (photo #6). Temporary E and S controls have been installed down gradient of the stormwater basin (photo #6). The EC of the soil down gradient of the stormwater basin was ~4.0 mS/cm. On 04/03/2026 an additional sump was installed further down gradient (photo #9). The additional sump is manned 24/7. Fluids are recovered from the sump ~ every hour. The EC of the fluids in the additional sump were ~1.4 mS/cm (1400 us/cm) (photo #10). The EC of fluids down gradient of the additional sump were between 101-104 us/cm. At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-529) UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the discharge the EC of the fluids were 71 us/cm (photo #13). The EC of the fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the confluence were ~ 935 us/cm (photo #14). At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-530) from UNT Rockwell Creek downstream of the discharge the EC of fluids were ~160 us/cm. As of 04/06/2026 5,293 barrels (166,729 gallons) have been recovered onsite. Resource management will continue screening and sampling ten monitoring points twice a week. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for EC between 430-640 us/cm. There was no evidence of any additional spills or releases. Proper secondary containment was observed throughout the site. Stimulation activities are to be continued until 04/30/2026.Violations remain open against API #015-23994. We departed at 1115 hours.

Violation ID: 848607
Permit API: 115-22398
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Jackson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-04-29
Comments: Today's inspection was conducted in response to SWN self-reporting of a spill identified initially by DTE and then reported to SWN. The spill occurred on the ROW of the DTE Susquehanna Gathering Well Connect 67 Pipeline at a waterline valve cellar located at latitude 41.876168 and longitude -75.583155 also located in Jackson Township. The waterline was installed by DTE but is owned and operated by SWN. On 4/25/19, DTE operations personnel were conducting an annual inspection of their Well Connect 67 Pipeline and identified a three quarter inch line with a leaking quarter turn ball relief valve located above the lid of the waterline valve cellar, as shown in Photo #1. Photo #2 shows the extent of the accelerated corrosion caused by the leak to the lid. The DTE Operations personnel then contacted their Operations management team who then contacted SWN's Production group at 1:30 PM, that same day, 4/25/19. On 4/26/19 at 1:40 PM, SWN confirmed that the water within the cellar did show elevated conductivity. On 4/26/19 at 3:01 PM, Mike Deming, SWN Senior Regulatory Analyst left a voice message on my cell phone. Mr. Deming then attempted to contact Briana Cunningham at 3:01 PM and left a voice message. At 3:05 PM, Briana Cunningham contacted Mike Deming by phone who then explained the conditions listed above and noted that their conductivity readings showed the conductivity of the water within the valve cellar to be above the meter's capability of 19.9 milli Siemens. SWN measured the soil conductivity just off the valve cellar lid where the leak was running off the lid to be at 6.27 milli Siemens. Among those personnel also present during the inspection today were Brianna Cunningham, Dept. WQSS, Eric Rooney, Dept. P.G., Jon Sassi, Dept. EPS, Cassidy Moyer, Dept. WQST, Mike Spangenberg, DTE Senior Environmental Manager, Mike Deming, SWN Senior Regulatory Analyst, Seth Tratthen, Senior Regulatory Analyst, Dawn Washo, Resource Environmental P.G., Project Manager, Abbey Vogler Resource Environmental G.I.T., Environmental Specialist, and Christian Mondi, Resource Environmental Data Specialist. Mike Deming stated that on 4/26/19 during the evening, 200 gallons of water was removed from the valve cellar. As Photo #1 shows, the valve cellar is made from a large corrugated pipe, and is designed to maintain the valve pit, but does not function as containment, as there is no bottom in this cellar. During the inspection, water was observed in the valve cellar, which is approximately 8' deep. Mike Deming stated that the water level in the cellar was at about the same height as it was on 4/25/19 when they removed and emptied the cellar, which would suggest that there is at least 200 gallons of water currently present in the cellar. Samples were collected from the valve cellar, a seep downgradient of the valve cellar, and samples collected from upstream and downstream of an ephemeral steam which the seep directly discharges to. Mike Spangenberg stated that prior to this leak discovery, DTE last inspected this line in June of 2018. Comments: On March 10 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the CFR/USX 5 OG Well in regards to OGI referral.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department traveled down the access road towards the well site. Approximately halfway down the access road, the Department observed water flowing onto the access road. The water was observed continuing to flow down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water.Upon further inspection, the water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet. Based on these observations, it appears the water is flowing from the drainage channel/trib to Antram Run onto the access road rather than through the culvert.Upon further inspection of the well site, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head, however had a previous operator listed (Apex Energy). No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead.A well posting was observed on a piece of production equipment and appeared to have all required information. However, it appeared damage and almost falling off. A production tank was observed onsite and appeared in sound condition. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface around the production tank.Prior to leaving the site the Department spoke with operator representative Heather Empfield and informed her of the E and S issues related to the access road caused by the flowing water as well as recommended a new well tag/well posting be installed at the well site.Ms. Empfield stated that she would contact the site foreman to inform them of the Department's observations and they would work to assess the site and correct any issues as necessary.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed erosion of the access road, failure to maintain the culvert, as well as failure to have the well properly posted.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/19/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/19/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 979234
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/19/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator about a release of an estimated 42 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and freshwater to the surface of pad B. The frac is on-going on Pad B. The site was snow-covered during this inspection. I met with EQT representative Zachary Subra upon arriving on Pad B. He showed me the location of the fluid discovered earlier in the day. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) present on the pad is in the northeast corner of the pad. The fluid on the pad surface is northeast of the MASS. The fluid in this area had an electrical conductivity (EC) of greater than 19.99 mS/cm. A thin layer of fluid covered approximately 20 square feet of the visible pad surface. The secondary containments for the heaters and pumps near this area of the pad had only snow and ice within them. The secondary containment at the southeast side of the MASS had fluid in it with EC of 700 to 1100 mS/cm. This containment appears to be in good condition and did not appear to be at risk of over-topping. Mr. Subra stated that there is also fluid with elevated EC at the northeast outlet of the north stormwater channel. The fluid was observed beginning at the east end of the rip rap at the end of the channel and extended for approximately 10-15ft farther to the northeast. This flow did not appear to reach the line of compost filter sock present approximately 5ft farther to the northeast. The fluid here ranged from 11.85 mS/cm to >19.99 mS/cm. The pad side slopes and the full length of the north stormwater channel was snow covered. The ground at the toe of the east pad side slope was also snow-covered and appeared frozen. Mr. Subra stated during the inspection that the suspected source of the fluid is the MASS since no other source could be identified. He stated that the space between the primary and secondary walls on the MASS contains fluid but the sensors on the MASS had not alerted them to elevated EC in this space. He also stated toward the end of this inspection that these sensors had been recalibrated and that they were now indicating that the fluid in this space has a high EC reading but he did not state what the reading was. I made the following recommendations to Mr. Subra during this inspection. The Department recommends not adding any additional fluid to the MASS. The Department recommends installing a sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel and collecting the fluid from this sump for the duration of the frac. The Department recommends emptying and disassembling the MASS. The Department recommends installing a trench, if possible, at the northeast corner of the pad to collect fluid before it makes its way into the north stormwater channel. The Department recommends monitoring this trench and the sump for electrical conductivity. I took sample 0718-197 from the east end of the north stormwater channel. I took sample 0718-198 from the northeast corner of the pad, next to the northeast side of the MASS. Both samples will be sent to the state laboratory. Sample 0718-197 will be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Br, and Li. Sample 0718-198 will be analyzed for the 942 metals plus Al, Br, and Li. On 12/20/22 Rick Hall of EQT emailed the Department a report detailing the results of EQT's investigation of the release. The report states, in summary, that a combination of things led to the release including a hole in the secondary containment liner of the interstitial space between each wall of the MASS, an incorrectly installed electrical conductivity meter in this space which lead to inconsistent readings, and a check valve installed backwards which led to a truck driver successfully off-loading produced fluid into the interstitial space. The report also stated that EQT is committed to pursuing remediation of this release under Act 2.Violations noted.

Comments: I met Chris Lee (Chesapeake) at the excavated area at the beginning of the access road who explained the following: This morning they finished excavating soil contaminated by a ~70 gallon diesel fuel release from a truck's tank. The excavated material is in containment further up the access road (photo). They collected soil samples and sent them to a lab today also. Chesapeake will go through Act 2 for cleanup standards. Comments: This well was inspected as part of a routine inspection. The well is currently awaiting a service rig, per the operator, and has not been recently pumped. It appears as though a leak occurred on this site sometime in the past year, and it was covered with absorbent peat and then left. The spill was not reported to DEP. The quantity of oil spilled is unknown, but appears to be greater than 5 gallons and less than one barrel. Oil stained soil with absorbent peat is noted in an L shape approximately 10 feet wide and 30 feet long that extends to the edge of the location. Absorbent peat is noted closer to the edge of the site, primarily. A small UNT of Briggs Run begins at the edge of the site. One oil soaked pad was noted in this ditch lone, although no oil was noted in the ditch at this time. The operator was contacted and they arrived on site to begin assessment and cleanup on 8/25. Per the operator, the spill occurred over this past winter and the well pumper covered the spill with peat sorb, which then settled as it was not cleaned up as the winter went on. Spring melt allowed the material to run to the edge of the site. Per the operator, the employee is no longer with the company. Cleanup should be completed in the next few days. Followup inspection will be performed at that time.The operator was also asked about the steep and rutted access roads on this lease and said that they have recently acquired a new bulldozer and intend to grade and fix lease roads soon.

Comments: In order to prevent further spread of COVID-19, Commonwealth offices are currently closed until April 30. During this time period, this inspector is working remotely to continue the mission of the Pennsylvania Department of Environment Protection. This administrative inspection is being conducted to document violations at the site. On 04/15/2020 Kyle Borden of CNX reported a 5 barrel produced fluid release from a valve in a 3" produced water line servicing the GH 122 well. On 04/16/2020 I spoke to Kyle Borden via phone. Borden indicated the spill is approximately 50' before the pad on the east side of the access road. The leak occurred in a 3” poly line valve that runs to the GH 68 tank battery, which services multiple wells. A well tender noticed the GH 68 tank battery wasn't receiving as much water as they expected. CNX checked all valves in lines feeding the GH 68 tank battery. Once they located the leak at the GH122 they shut down the wells and blew down the brine line. As of 04/16/2020 CNX estimates the spill is 60% remediated. Borden indicated CNX will be remediating via alternate method and may pursue Act 2 for release of liability. CNX indicated they will provide the Department a notification within 15 days of the spill if CNX determines to utilize Act 2.

Comments: On March 5, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection at the Oliver East well pad in Forward Township, Allegheny County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3913651. IR 3913651 was conducted in response to the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure which reportedly released 5-10 gallons of produced water to the surface of the well pad. Notice of Termination request was approved by the Department for this site on November 10, 2022.The following was observed:The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 21). The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 22). The well pad appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 1). Sediment from the access road appears to threaten a stormwater drain along Williamsport Road (see photo 23). Although no sediment was observed inside this stormwater drain at the time of inspection, a layer of sediment was observed on debris that had accumulated on top of the storm drain grate.The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 3). Well 4H is equipped with a well tag with no evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be equipped for production (see photos 5 and 6). There are fourteen additional well heads onsite that also appear to be in production (see photo 4). An additional storage tank placed within secondary containment was observed onsite (see photo 7). This secondary containment appears to be holding a significant amount of rainwater at the time of inspection. Old GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 9). However, their associated wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. New GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 8).A reported absorbent material has been applied to the majority of the area impacted by the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure (see photos 10-12). The conductivity of the soil underneath this reported absorbent material remains significantly higher than the surrounding soil (see photos 13-20). The soil conductivity meter utilized for this inspection was calibrated immediately prior to conducting this inspection. Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that not all impacted material has been removed and therefore remediation appears to be incomplete. Because it appears that not all impacted material has been removed and greater than 15 days has passed since the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure occurred, violations shall be issued in this inspection report.The Department continues to recommend that secondary containments are kept empty so they are able to function as intended in the event of a release. The Department also recommends that the operator take immediate measures to address and prevent potential pollution due to sediment discharge from the access road to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

Permit API: 053-29526
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with rods and tubing. The pump jack has been removed from the well, the annulus of the well remains connected to a gathering line. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. The well is not equipped with a well tag, nor is there a site ID sign posted at the location.A tank battery containing four steel tanks and two poly tanks inside of an earthen containment is located approximately 200 feet east of this well. There are indications that production fluids (primarily brine) have repeatedly been released onto the gravel inside of this containment. The soil is stained and specific conductance of the soil is elevated at the western edge where fluid from the tanks appears to have been released, and at the eastern edge of the containment where fluids appear to have been released from a pipeline riser/blow off).Vegetation is absent and deer tracks are very dense on the surface outside of the west/northwest extent of the containment, as it appears the released fluids have migrated through the earthen walls at the natural contour onto which the gravel and earthen wells were constructed. Stained soil and elevated specific conductance continue westward into a roadside ditch of Forest Road 219 until the ditch reaches a cross culvert approximately 300 feet away.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29931, 053-29930, 053-29944, 053-29955 and 053-29945 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. These E and S concerns are considered part of E and S violations that are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29816 (Warrant 2980 #45).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/19/2023 to CRS ENERGY LLC in Greenwood Twp, Crawford county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CRS ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/19/2023
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 992219
Permit API: 039-23713
Unconventional: No
County: Crawford
Municipality: Greenwood Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/19/2023
Comments: Onsite for a routine inspection. There is a 100bbl steel tank, 50bbl steel tank, and a separator located inside and earthen dike. The well is labeled and a house gas meter is plumbed to the well. Production for 2022 was reported as 758mcf for the year.The heater tube on the 100bbl steel take is actively leaking fluid. The operator was contacted via phone and it was stated that a water truck would be called ASAP to have the tank emptied and the heater tube would be plugged.4/20/2023I received a text from the operator with photos showing that the heater tube was plugged and not leaking.The violation(s) were immediately corrected at the site.A follow-up inspection will be conducted by the Department to confirm compliance.
